lead: >-
  The Holandes Cays are part of our eight-day yacht journey through the Panama Canal and the San Blas Islands. The yacht reaches the Holandes reefs on day 5, after Coco Bandero; the next stop is Isla Perro, with a shipwreck just offshore. We explain the remote archipelago's place in the itinerary, what is planned on the islands, how the passages are arranged and what to consider before choosing a yacht trip.

## How to Visit the Holandes Cays on a Tour

The [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/) are a group of small Caribbean islands in the [San Blas](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) region of Guna Yala. Travelers come for island scenery, shallow reefs and time on the water. Unlike a holiday focused on staying at one beach, a yacht itinerary allows you to see several islands by moving from one anchorage to another.

Our current catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. On our itinerary, the Holandes Cays are visited on **day 5** of an eight-day yacht cruise. The opening days are devoted to boarding, transiting the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) and sailing to San Blas; after Holandes, the route continues to other islands.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_ostrova_san_blas_na_yakhte_lyuks_klassa}}

The [San Blas Islands Yacht Tour, Panama](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/) suits those who want the sea voyage to be the main part of the vacation. It lasts **8 days and 7 nights**, rather than being a standalone day trip to Holandes. Accommodation is aboard the yacht. Detailed charter terms, price and services should be compared using this particular product's listing.

## Day 5 Among the Holandes Reefs

After visiting [Coco Bandero Island](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/), the yacht heads toward the more remote Holandes islands. The program describes reef-sheltered waters, clear seas and an anchorage near a natural shallow pool between the islands. Swimming, possible fishing and a barbecue ashore are planned.

The route also includes an introduction to the northern section of the reef. This provides an opportunity to see marine life from the boat and while snorkeling, weather and sea conditions permitting. Access to any particular reef section depends on the captain's decision, wave conditions and safety; the description should not be taken as a guarantee that every small island will be visited.

Panama's tourism portal identifies Cayos Holandeses as a remote group of islands of particular interest for snorkeling. **The main reason to choose this section** is its combination of reef scenery and a longer sea passage. Eight days on a yacht make it possible to include this anchorage in a sequence of islands, rather than limiting the trip to one beach.

## How Holandes Connects to the Other San Blas Stops

Comparing neighboring days of the itinerary is helpful: the experiences differ even though all these places belong to Panama's Caribbean coast.

| Stop | Main Activity in the Program |
| --- | --- |
| [El Porvenir](/panama/place/el-porvenir-island/) | Island visit and permit formalities |
| [Coco Bandero](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/) | Shallow water and transparent kayak |
| [Holandes](/panama/place/holandes-cays/) | Reefs, anchorage and barbecue |
| [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) | Snorkeling near a shipwreck |
| [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) | Island walk and relaxation |

For travelers, this means changing scenery without having to return to the capital every day. On [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/), the focus is the shipwreck near shore; at Holandes, it is the reefs and island waters. The pages for these two places therefore help you choose different experiences **within one confirmed tour**, not two independent Ada Tours programs.

The journey begins in [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), with yacht boarding near [Flamenco Island](/panama/place/flamenco-island/). On day 2, the yacht transits the canal to [Shelter Bay](/panama/place/shelter-bay/) on the Atlantic side. The trip concludes with a return to Panama; a flight on a small aircraft is planned for the final day. Details of this flight and the transfers should be confirmed for the chosen charter, as the general inclusions do not specify their complete pricing.

## Preparing for a Yacht Stop

**Water and sunshine.** For repeated trips onto the deck, pack a hat, light clothing covering the shoulders, water and reliable sun protection. For snorkeling, bringing your own well-fitting equipment may be best if the yacht's available gear and sizes have not yet been confirmed.

**Reef safety.** Coral and shallow areas need careful treatment: do not stand on a living reef or take a boat too close to it. Swimming time, fishing, kayaking and landing ashore depend on local rules and the conditions of each anchorage. Snorkeling in the program must not automatically be equated with scuba diving.

**Guna Yala rules.** The islands are part of a territory governed by the Guna people. Vessel calls, shore visits and photography or video recording in communities are subject to local rules. The yacht program provides for immigration and cruise permits during the stop at El Porvenir. These formalities do not replace checking each traveler's documents for their nationality and route of arrival.

**Weather and sea.** Access to remote islands is particularly dependent on wind and waves. If a specific reef section is the purpose of the trip, discuss in advance with the organizer how much flexibility there is in the order of anchorages. Descriptions of clear water and reefs characterize the place but do not promise identical visibility every day.

## Who Will Enjoy a Journey Through Holandes?

A yacht trip is worth choosing if you want to spend several nights at sea and explore the San Blas islands in sequence. The passages themselves, life aboard and opportunities to anchor by reefs are central to the experience. For someone with only one day in Panama, the full eight-day route would be excessive; a better starting point is the [Panama tours catalog](/panama/tour/) to compare trip lengths.

Our yacht tour includes **accommodation aboard and island excursions**. International flights are excluded. The VIP designation in the tour name does not by itself guarantee a particular yacht model, number of cabins, complete range of water equipment or additional services unless these are expressly stated in the terms. It is best to confirm such details before paying.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I visit Holandes on a separate one-day Ada Tours excursion?

Our current catalog presents Holandes as part of the [eight-day yacht itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/). A separate one-day Ada Tours product for these islands is not confirmed here.

### On which day does the yacht reach Holandes?

Day 5, after the anchorage at Coco Bandero. The following day is devoted to Isla Perro. This order follows the current itinerary description, but conditions at sea may require changes.

### Is scuba diving available at Holandes?

The stop description confirms swimming, exploring the reef and possible fishing. Organized scuba dives are not listed as included services. For underwater experiences, plan around snorkeling and check current local restrictions separately.

### Where do participants sleep?

Accommodation is aboard the yacht for all seven nights. An overnight hotel stay on Holandes itself is not listed.

### Are Holandes and Isla Perro visits on the same tour?

Yes. Both stops are included in the [same San Blas itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/), on separate days with different water activities.

## Panama Attractions: How to Choose Places for Your Trip

Many visitors begin exploring Panama with [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) and the famous [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). Yet the country combines a modern Pacific city, historic districts, cloud forests in the Chiriquí mountains, Caribbean archipelagos and protected Pacific islands. To see what really motivates your journey, start by grouping the attractions by geography and travel time.

The [Panama destinations catalog](/panama/) brings together urban, natural and coastal places. Here you can learn where to focus your first few days, where to go after the capital and which excursions usually require a separate overnight stay.

## Panama City: Old Town, Canal and Museums

The capital is the most convenient place to begin. In [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), you can bring together several eras: skyscrapers beside the bay, a walking tour through [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/) and views of ships passing through the canal.

**Casco Viejo** is a historic district with squares, old facades and bay views. According to Panama's tourism portal, the neighborhood dates back to 1673 and forms part of a UNESCO World Heritage property. It is best explored on foot, with stops at the squares and architectural landmarks. The [Biomuseo](/panama/place/biomuseo/), which covers the biodiversity of the Panamanian isthmus, is a good introduction to the country's natural world.

**The Panama Canal** deserves its own engineering-focused excursion. At the [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/), travelers watch the system that connects ocean shipping routes in operation. If the Caribbean side appeals to you, consider the [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/) and [Gatun Lake](/panama/place/gatun-lake/), although a visit there requires more time on the road.

| Area | Why Visit |
|---|---|
| Casco Viejo | History, squares, architecture |
| Canal locks | Ships and engineering |
| Biomuseo | Nature of the Panamanian isthmus |
| Gatun Lake | Water, forest and canal |

## Nature Near the Capital

Forested areas close to Panama City can be visited without crossing the entire country. [Soberanía National Park](/panama/place/soberania-national-park/) is known for tropical forest and birdwatching. [Gamboa](/panama/place/gamboa/) is near the canal and Gatun Lake, making the area a convenient base for nature excursions.

For those who want to experience the forest from the water, the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/) and nature routes in [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) are appealing. When visiting [Emberá communities along the Chagres](/panama/place/embera-chagres-community/), agree on the format of the reception beforehand and respect local customs. A cultural visit to a community and wildlife observation are different activities; choose the duration and transport according to your purpose.

These attractions can make a separate day trip from the capital, but proximity on a map does not always mean a short journey. Some locations require water transport, and weather affects trail conditions.

## Boquete and the Chiriquí Highlands

[Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) in western Panama has a cooler highland climate than the capital. Visitors travel here for mountain walks, coffee farms and natural scenery. Panama's tourism authority highlights the region's coffee culture, waterfalls, hiking trails and active pursuits.

If mountains interest you, consider [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/). Such an excursion requires preparation, checking access and assessing physical ability; a famous natural attraction is not necessarily an easy walk for every group.

It is best to allow a distinct portion of the journey for Boquete. One night gives only a quick impression of the area, while several days allow you to add coffee experiences, forest and nature trails without constantly moving between places.

## Islands and Beaches: San Blas or Bocas del Toro?

Two different destinations stand out in the Caribbean. The [San Blas archipelago](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) is known for small islands, white beaches and its connection to Guna territory and culture. When organizing a visit, consider local rules, sea transport and weather dependence.

[Bocas del Toro](/panama/place/bocas-del-toro/) offers a different kind of Caribbean coast, with islands and beach areas where relaxation, boat outings and nature excursions can be combined. Its distance from the capital makes it difficult to treat as a short outing from the city.

For a quiet island day nearer the capital, consider [Taboga Island](/panama/place/taboga-island/) in the Pacific. When choosing a beach, look beyond the water color in photographs to actual travel time, boat schedules, seasonal waves and accommodation options.

## Dividing Destinations by Trip Length

For a short first visit, start with the capital, [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/), the Panama Canal and one nature excursion. With more time, add one more distant region: mountainous [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) or the Caribbean islands. Trying to include every destination within a few days will turn the journey into a succession of transfers.

Seasonality also matters. Rainfall and sea conditions can differ between Panama's Pacific and Caribbean coasts, while mountain weather changes quickly. Check the travel conditions and transport access to a chosen island before fixing the entire itinerary.

[Panama tours](/panama/tour/) let you compare ready-made combinations of the country's attractions. We can also arrange a private itinerary, but the specific included services, boats, entrance tickets and accommodation depend on the program selected.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Places in Panama

### What should I definitely see on a first trip to Panama?

Most visitors start with historic [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/), the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) locks and one natural area. Then choose between islands and mountains according to your interests.

### Where can I see tropical forest without a long drive?

Near the capital are [Soberanía](/panama/place/soberania-national-park/), [Gamboa](/panama/place/gamboa/) and the Chagres River region. The type of visit depends on the route and whether a boat is needed.

### How does Boquete differ from San Blas?

[Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) means mountains, coffee and walks. [San Blas](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) means islands, sea and local Guna culture. They involve different climate zones and ways of traveling.

### Can I combine the Atlantic and Pacific coasts?

Yes. Panama has shores on both ocean basins. The specific combination, however, depends on time, transport and weather; two coasts that appear close on a map are not always a quick journey apart.

## Isla Perro: A San Blas Island with a Shipwreck

**Isla Perro (Perro Chico)** is a small island in the [San Blas archipelago](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) off the Caribbean coast of [Panama](/panama/). Its most recognizable attraction is underwater: a shipwreck lies just offshore, providing habitat for reef fish.

Travelers come for a combination of **snorkeling and a short beach break**. Water clarity and depth vary with weather and exact location, so a rewarding underwater view is never guaranteed by the name of the island alone.

## What You Can See Underwater

The wreck's frame provides shelter for fish, and marine organisms grow on parts of its surface. With good visibility, snorkelers can make out the outline of the ship while remaining near the surface. The current Ada Tours itinerary description mentions an area roughly 5–6 meters deep; the actual depth at the chosen entry point may differ.

Swimming right up to the wreck is dangerous: metal and coral may have sharp edges. **Do not enter the ship**, touch its structure or take objects from the seabed. Reef sections are easily damaged, even when a visitor simply stands on them.

Watching marine life at Isla Perro differs from an ordinary beach walk: account for waves, currents, strong sunlight and your own swimming ability.

## Snorkeling and Scuba Diving Are Different Activities

To explore the wreck in shallow water, travelers most often choose **snorkeling**, swimming at the surface with a mask and snorkel. Scuba diving is a separate service with different requirements. A maritime attraction in the itinerary does not mean scuba dives with tanks or an instructor are available at Isla Perro.

Local sources on San Blas describe the area primarily as a snorkeling destination. If organized diving is your priority, first compare [diving itineraries](/interests/diving/) and check that the required activity is included in the chosen program.

Before going into the water, establish whether everyone can swim, whether the vessel provides suitable masks, who supervises safety and whether participants can stay on the shore instead of swimming.

## Isla Perro and Nearby Islands

Nearby stops on marine itineraries include the [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/), [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) and [Coco Bandero](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/). Each is visited for a different reason: some for an underwater feature, others for a beach or views from the boat.

| Place | Main Attraction |
|---|---|
| Isla Perro | Shipwreck and snorkeling |
| [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) | Beach and reefs |
| [Holandes](/panama/place/holandes-cays/) | Island anchorages |

All lie within the Guna Yala region. Local communities have their own rules for landing, staying and taking photographs. Do not feed fish, damage corals or leave litter.

## Isla Perro on an Ada Tours Yacht Journey

We have made Isla Perro a separate stop on our [eight-day San Blas yacht itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/). The tour includes sea passages, islands and nights aboard the yacht. At Isla Perro, the plan is to explore the shipwreck and have an opportunity to snorkel.

Before booking, check what equipment is actually provided, how much time is allowed on the island and how the marine itinerary changes in poor weather. Describing the trip as VIP does not guarantee specific equipment.

## When to Go and How to Prepare

Panama's dry season is generally convenient for travel from December to March, but Caribbean winds and water clarity can change during any month. Even a short water excursion requires attention to the forecast and the captain's decisions.

Bring sun protection and suitable water equipment if the operator does not provide it. Beginners should choose a calm entry point and stay close to their guide. Watching fish is rewarding in itself; there is no need to swim close enough to touch the wreck.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Isla Perro

### Where is the shipwreck?

It lies just off Isla Perro in the San Blas archipelago. The captain chooses the precise viewing spot according to conditions on the water.

### Do you need a diving certificate?

No diving certificate is required for snorkeling. Scuba diving is a separate activity with its own requirements and preparation.

### Can I stay ashore instead of swimming?

Yes, provided the anchorage allows a landing. Choose water activities according to your skills and the actual weather.

## Which Tour Includes Isla Perro?

[Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) is among the [San Blas](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) islands on Panama's Caribbean side. Its main attraction for visitors is **the shipwreck near shore**, visible from the water's surface with a mask. Corals and reef fish can be seen on and around the hull. That gives travelers a specific reason to stop here, even if the yacht has already visited beautiful beaches on earlier days.

The current catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Our offer is an **eight-day yacht journey through the Panama Canal and the San Blas Islands**. Isla Perro is scheduled for **day 6**, between the [Holandes Cays](/panama/place/holandes-cays/) and [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_ostrova_san_blas_na_yakhte_lyuks_klassa}}

The [San Blas yacht tour](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/) is worth considering if you want to spend several nights aboard and visit different islands. The shipwreck stop forms part of the voyage's sequence; we do not offer a separate short excursion solely to Isla Perro here.

## What Happens on the Day at the Shipwreck?

According to the day-at-sea description, the yacht approaches Isla Perro, where a wrecked ship lies in shallow water. At low tide, parts of the structure may appear above the surface; when the water is higher, visitors can view it with a mask and snorkel. Corals and fish live around the hull, and the site has become a notable snorkeling spot in San Blas.

**The main activity here is observing from the surface**, not going inside the wreck. Even if the water looks calm, stay within the area indicated by the captain, watch for other boats and avoid touching metal parts. The hull may have sharp edges, while corals are easily damaged. How close you can safely approach depends on waves, currents, water clarity and the crew's instructions.

San Blas sources often refer to this attraction as the wreck off Perro Chico. Accounts differ about the circumstances of its loss, so it is more reliable to focus on the confirmed place being visited than on an unverified shipwreck story. Confirm the exact anchorage and swimming conditions when arranging the itinerary.

## How Isla Perro Differs from Holandes and Coco Bandero

The tour includes several stops with swimming and underwater experiences, but each has its own main focus.

| Island | Main Experience |
| --- | --- |
| [Coco Bandero](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/) | Reef, kayak, swimming |
| [Holandes](/panama/place/holandes-cays/) | Remote reefs and anchorage |
| [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) | Shipwreck |
| [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) | Beach and island walk |

On day four, the yacht is at Coco Bandero, with snorkeling and a chance to use a transparent kayak. Day five is spent near the more remote Holandes Cays, with a reef anchorage and barbecue. On day six, the emphasis shifts to Isla Perro's specific underwater feature. Day seven brings travelers to Turtle Island.

This comparison helps determine your priorities. All stops are interesting for island photography from the deck; Coco Bandero and Holandes appeal to reef enthusiasts; **Isla Perro is the key day for snorkeling by a wreck**.

## How the Journey to Isla Perro Is Arranged

The sea voyage begins in [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). On day one, travelers are met at the airport and transferred to [Flamenco Island](/panama/place/flamenco-island/) to board the yacht. On day two, the vessel transits the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) toward [Shelter Bay](/panama/place/shelter-bay/), then heads to the San Blas Islands.

At [El Porvenir](/panama/place/el-porvenir-island/), the captain handles immigration documents and cruise permits. After several island anchorages, the yacht reaches Isla Perro. The journey ends with a return to Panama on the final day, which describes a flight on a small aircraft. Because this portion is not itemized in the general list of paid services, the flight price, baggage and connection conditions need separate confirmation.

**Seven nights are spent aboard the yacht.** The approved itinerary does not list a hotel on Isla Perro or daily trips there from Panama City. That distinguishes this program from one-day San Blas excursions offered by other operators, which are not part of Ada Tours' currently confirmed selection.

## What to Bring for Snorkeling Near the Island

**Mask and snorkel.** Confirm in advance what equipment is available aboard, including sizes for children and adults. A poorly fitting mask makes even a shallow site uncomfortable. Fins and a life jacket should also be discussed with the crew; their availability cannot be inferred from the word "snorkeling" alone.

**Safety.** Metal wreckage, corals and passing boats require a safe distance. Do not enter cavities in the wrecked hull or lean against it. Swim within the zone specified by the crew and do not enter the water without the captain's approval.

**Scuba and freediving.** The tour description mentions visiting the wreck, but a separately licensed diving program, tanks, an instructor and a complete set of equipment are not confirmed as included services. Guna Yala has its own restrictions on recreational sea activities. Do not assume tank diving is available without explicit confirmation.

**Weather.** Visibility, currents and water levels change, and landing or swimming may depend on conditions. If underwater photography is your primary reason for traveling, discuss the feasibility and duration of the stop with the organizer before booking. Neither clear water nor sightings of specific fish are guaranteed.

## Choosing an Itinerary with Isla Perro

This yacht tour suits travelers interested in **several different islands in one trip**, including reefs, beaches and the underwater attraction near Isla Perro. Being comfortable spending nights aboard and adapting marine activities to the weather matters. Our yacht tour includes accommodation aboard and island excursions; international flights cost extra.

If you are planning a short introduction to the country, compare other [Panama tours](/panama/tour/). If an itinerary combining island passages and relaxation aboard a yacht appeals to you, open the [full San Blas program](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/) and confirm the charter's inclusions, cabin count, transfers and equipment. A VIP label in the program title does not automatically establish that every one of these services is included.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### On which day does the tour visit Isla Perro?

On **day 6** of the eight-day trip. The previous day is devoted to Holandes and the next to Turtle Island.

### Do I need to be a diver to see the wreck?

Snorkeling with a mask and snorkel is used to view it from the surface. Diver certification is not a stated requirement for this stop. Scuba diving should not be considered an included service.

### Can you enter the wreck?

The program includes a visit to the underwater attraction near the island, but entering the sunken hull is not listed. For safety, do not enter the structure or touch its sharp edges.

### Are Isla Perro and the Holandes Cays included in different tours?

No. In the current catalog, both are stops on the [same San Blas yacht tour](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/), on separate days.

### Where can I find the price for this trip?

The price and confirmed terms appear on the [yacht tour page](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/). Before paying, check how the price is calculated, crew and equipment inclusions, and whether flights and transfers are covered.

## Miraflores Locks: Watching the Panama Canal at Work

The Miraflores Locks are one of the clearest ways to experience the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). Huge seagoing vessels pass through narrow chambers, the water rises or falls, and the gates open the way to the next stretch. Visitors can watch all this from the visitor center near [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/).

Miraflores is especially interesting for people who want to understand how the canal operates. Seeing a ship against the lock walls is impressive even without engineering knowledge, but understanding the chambers makes the experience far more meaningful. Allow a separate part of the day for the visit: ship transits, exhibitions and views from the platforms depend on vessel traffic and the complex's current operating conditions.

## How the Miraflores Locks Work

The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans through a series of waterways and locks. Ships do not travel along a continuously level channel. The central section passes through Gatun Lake, which is above sea level; the locks allow vessels to rise to the lake's elevation and descend again toward the other ocean.

Miraflores is on the Pacific side of the canal's original lock system. It has two successive stages of locking. A vessel enters a chamber, massive gates close, and the water level changes to the next level. Water moves primarily by gravity. Once the levels are equalized, the gates open and the vessel moves onward.

Several details are worth watching: the gap between the ship's hull and the chamber walls, the movement of the gates, changes in water level and the work of the teams assisting the vessel. Together, these operations show how an oceangoing ship overcomes a difference in elevation.

## What to See at the Visitor Center

### Viewing Platforms Over the Lock Chambers

The observation areas overlook the chambers and approaching ships. Watching the full cycle is particularly rewarding when a ship enters and the water level begins to change. Exact times and the number of ship transits, however, depend on the shipping schedule. A visit does not guarantee that a particular cruise ship or container vessel will appear at a chosen moment.

For photography, it helps to be able to change vantage points: wide shots show the entire mechanism, while closer views reveal the gates and the ship's dimensions. Facilities and the availability of viewing areas may change during technical work.

### Construction History and Canal Engineering

The visitor center supplements the views with the history of the canal's construction and explanations of its operation. It is an opportunity to connect what you see of modern engineering with the way the waterway transformed maritime routes between oceans. Check the exhibition format, film access and individual halls on the official website before visiting, as the center underwent modernization in 2026.

It is important to distinguish the lock complex itself from the visitor center's tourist program. Even with an admission ticket, a visit does not become a trip aboard a ship or a voyage along the entire canal.

## Miraflores and the New Locks: What Is the Difference?

Miraflores belongs to the historic locks of the Panama Canal, opened in 1914. Following the expansion in 2016, additional lock complexes were built for larger vessels, including Cocolí on the Pacific side. Different classes of ships use the original and new chambers.

Two similar promotional photographs of the canal may therefore show different sites. If you specifically want to see the largest NeoPanamax ships, visiting historic Miraflores alone cannot promise that experience: those vessels use the expanded system. For learning how locks work, by contrast, the original chambers are particularly useful because of their clear stepped design and observation platforms.

For a fuller geographic explanation, see our article on the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/), which also discusses the role of [Gatun Lake](/panama/place/gatun-lake/).

## Combining Miraflores with a Walk Through the Capital

Miraflores is commonly included in an introduction to [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). The day can then continue to the [Biomuseo](/panama/place/biomuseo/) and historic [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/). This is a substantial combination: the engineering history of the canal, the nature of the Panamanian isthmus and colonial architecture.

That is how day two of the [Panama City and Gamboa: Canal, Forest and Emberá in 6 Days tour](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/) is organized. Visiting the locks is part of an excursion day covering capital attractions. Exact tickets and the order of stops are determined by the tour itinerary rather than general information about the visitor center.

For a separate introduction to this part of the city, there is the [Miraflores, Biomuseo and Casco Viejo excursion](/panama/panama-city/panama-miraflores-biomuseo-casco-viejo/). Another option is [Panama City: Miraflores, IMAX and Amador](/panama/panama-city/panama-city-miraflores-imax-amador/), which features a different set of visits. When selecting an excursion, compare its confirmed stops and included services.

## Practical Tips Before Visiting

Ship movements and visitor-accessible areas change independently of tourist plans. Check the center's current opening hours, how to purchase admission, viewing-platform access and any restrictions due to renovation. Decide in advance how important it is to see an actual ship transit: the excursion timing can then be matched to the center's opportunities, although there is still no absolute guarantee.

Panama is warm and humid. Drinking water, sun protection and comfortable shoes are useful when moving between indoor and outdoor areas. For photographs of ships, leave some space around the vessel in the frame; this makes its dimensions relative to the chamber more apparent.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Miraflores Locks

### Can you watch ships lock through from the shore without boarding a vessel?

Yes. Part of the purpose of the Miraflores visitor center is to let people observe the locks at work. Visibility of particular stages and access to platforms depend on current operations.

### Do all Panama Canal ships pass through Miraflores?

No. Vessels are distributed between the historic and expanded lock systems. Large NeoPanamax ships use the new system.

### Can you also visit Gatun Lake and Monkey Island?

Yes, on a broader Panama journey, but they require a separate boat program from [Gamboa](/panama/place/gamboa/). On the [six-day Ada Tours itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/), the locks are scheduled for day two, while [Monkey Island](/panama/place/monkey-island-gatun/) is on day five.

### Do you need to buy tickets in advance?

Ticket-purchasing conditions can change. Check the visitor center's official website before travel and coordinate the date with the actual excursion schedule.
